Specify priors for phase model

Source: R/prior.R
prior.Rd

Creates a prior specification object with either simple SD parameters or full distribution specifications using formula syntax.

Usage

prior(..., beta_sd = 2.5, sigma_sd = 1, re_sd = 0.5)

Arguments

...

Prior specifications using formula syntax (e.g., beta ~ normal(0, 2.5)) or named SD parameters for backward compatibility (beta_sd = 2.5).

beta_sd

Prior SD for regression coefficients (default 2.5, ignored if formula syntax is used)

sigma_sd

Prior SD for log(sigma) parameters (default 1, ignored if formula syntax is used)

re_sd

Prior SD for random effect hyperparameter (default 0.5, ignored if formula syntax is used)

Value

A phase_prior object

Details

The default priors are weakly informative:

  • Regression coefficients: Normal(0, 2.5)

  • Residual SD (sigma): Half-Normal(0, 1)

  • Random effect SD: Half-Normal(0, 0.5)

  • Correlation (LKJ): LKJ(2)

Supported distributions

normal(mean, sd)

Normal distribution

student_t(df, mean, scale)

Student-t distribution

cauchy(location, scale)

Cauchy distribution

half_normal(sd)

Half-Normal (positive values only)

half_cauchy(scale)

Half-Cauchy (positive values only)

lkj(eta)

LKJ prior for correlation matrices

Parameter classes

beta

All regression coefficients (fixed effects)

sigma

Residual standard deviations

re

Random effect standard deviations

cor

Correlation matrices (for correlated random slopes)

Examples

# Default priors
prior()

# Simple SD specification (backward compatible)
prior(beta_sd = 1)

# Full distribution specification
prior(
  beta ~ normal(0, 2.5),
  sigma ~ half_cauchy(1),
  re ~ half_normal(0.5),
  cor ~ lkj(2)
)

# Student-t for robust regression coefficients
prior(beta ~ student_t(3, 0, 2.5))
